newsitem.title: USA: Clinton urges end to violence in Gaza, West Bank.
newsitem.headline: Clinton urges end to violence in Gaza, West Bank.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Thursday he has asked both Israel and the Palestinians to "end the violence" and resume peace negotiations.

"I asked both sides to end this violence, to get back to the business of the peace ... to resolve their differences through negotiations," Clinton said in his first public statement on violence raging the past two days between Israelis and Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza.

"I deeply regret the injuries and loss of life we've seen in the West Bank and Gaza in the last two days. It points to the urgency of both sides not only to end the violence but to take positive steps to resolve the issues that divide them," Clinton said in a statement read to reporters as he left the White House for a visit to Congress.

Clinton said he had urged the two sides "to avoid unnecessarily provocative actions." He said U.S. officials including Secretary of State Warren Christopher had been in touch with Israeli and Palestinian leaders since the violence erupted.

Arab anger at Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's failure to extend self-rule in the West Bank and Gaza boiled over on Wednesday when his right-wing government opened an archaeological tunnel near Moslem holy places in Jerusalem. The fierce fighting shook U.S. hopes of keeping alive Arab-Israeli peace talks, stalled since Netanyahu came to power 100 days ago.
At least 35 Palestinians and 11 Israelis had been reported killed by Thursday.
